corrections: wn30-n-05624700: The creativity gloss only restates the headword as the ability to create, without explaining originality or the production of new ideas or forms.
wn30-n-05673209: The forgetfulness gloss only restates the headword as a tendency to forget without explaining failures of memory or recall.

wn30-n-05697976: The trust/reliance gloss requires certainty based on past experience, although reliance can involve uncertainty and need not be based on prior experience; it overstates confidence as certainty.
wn30-n-05698247: The definition only restates the headword as unsure without independently explaining the epistemic state.
wn30-n-05708432: The perception gloss only restates the headword as the process of perceiving, without explaining sensory awareness or interpretation.

wn30-n-05795044: The arrangement/agreement gloss only restates the headwords as the thing arranged or agreed to; it does not independently describe a plan, disposition, or mutually accepted understanding.

wn30-n-05861317: The unrestricted mathematical degree gloss gives a highest power without specifying degree in a variable versus total degree; for a multivariate term total degree sums exponents rather than taking the highest. See https://doc.cgal.org/4.5.2/Polynomial/index.html.

wn30-n-05862410: The monic-polynomial gloss omits the defining requirement that the leading coefficient is one, falsely equating monic with univariate. See https://eceweb.uwaterloo.ca/~dwharder/Algorithmic_thinking/Polynomial_arithmetic/.

wn30-n-05867283: The geometric vertex gloss calls any intersection of lines a vertex and gives no incidence with the edges of the relevant figure; it is too broad to distinguish a vertex from an arbitrary crossing.

wn30-n-05922949: The reference gloss conflates a word's meaning with the class of objects it denotes and does not distinguish the relation of referring from its referents. See https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/frege/.
wn30-n-05952490: The supernaturalism gloss makes forces beyond ordinary understanding sufficient, conflating unexplained natural phenomena with belief in a supernatural realm or agency.
wn30-n-06008609: The axis gloss says only that a line satisfies certain unspecified conditions; without naming the conditions it fails to distinguish an axis from other lines through a figure.

wn30-n-06023969: The mean gloss leaves both functions unspecified, so it supplies no computable mathematical definition and would permit arbitrary quantities unrelated to a mean. See https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/eda/section3/eda351.htm.

wn30-n-06029306: The regression-line gloss treats an arbitrary smooth fitted curve as a line, conflating regression curves with the straight-line special case. See https://itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/pmd/section8/pmd8111.htm.

wn30-n-06056923: The psychotherapy gloss treats it exclusively as a branch of psychiatry, obscuring that psychological treatment is provided by several mental-health professions. See https://www.nimh.nih.gov/health/topics/psychotherapies.

wn30-n-06094587: The physical-science gloss lists properties, phenomena, and laws rather than describing a discipline studying the material world; it confuses the subject matter with the science. See https://ncses.nsf.gov/surveys/federal-funds-research-development/2021.

wn30-n-06136258: The historical psychology gloss limits the discipline to mental life, omitting its study of behavior and its biological, social, and environmental contexts. See https://www.apa.org/ed/precollege/topss/science/overview.
